Colorectal cancer (kolorektalkræft) is a severe and frequent complication within the context of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) management in Denmark. According to the DANIBD national quality database report, it remains one of the most common causes of death among patients with IBD [^src1]. The risk is especially pronounced for patients who also suffer from [[psc|Primær skleroserende kolangitis (PSC)]], as they face a markedly increased risk of developing colorectal cancer compared to the general IBD population [^src1]. 

Due to this elevated mortality risk, colorectal cancer is officially documented as a leading [[doedsaarsag|doedsaarsag]] (cause of death) in these patient groups [^src1]. To address this, the Danish healthcare system has implemented systematic surveillance colonoscopies as a crucial preventative strategy. This effort is tracked under Indicator 7 of the DANIBD quality monitoring framework, which specifically mandates regular colonoscopies for PSC patients to detect and prevent colorectal cancer, thereby ensuring equitable, evidence-based care across all Danish regions and departments [^src1].
